The CV’s reviewing venues and manuscript target venues are real journals. The document-level fiction notice does not satisfy the requested no-real-identity policy for these invented affiliations, service, awards and projects. PID2024 is listed in Annex V and HEATPOL ends in August 2028. Choosing type B does not remove that incompatibility. Separately, the claimed real PID2024 award uses a 21% indirect-cost rate, whereas the scheme prescribes 25%. The existing 21% arithmetic is correct, but its attribution to PID2024 is not. These are defects in the dossier’s funding history, not additional intended traps.
issues.fix: Recast the active award as a fictional institutional grant from the fictional host: “PB-FILATHERM, reference PB-CESERAL-2025-01, Institutional Emerging Groups Programme (fictional), 1 September 2025–31 August 2028; EUR 150000 direct plus EUR 31500 indirect, total EUR 181500. The 21% indirect rate is a condition of this fictional award. Its terms permit participation in other projects, subject to compatible effort and no double funding.” Replace the AEI/PID2024 attribution in the report, CV and F03/F22; keep dates, direct-cost rows, expenditure and total arithmetic. Replace the linked “FPI” contract with a separately funded institutional predoctoral contract, retaining October 2025–September 2029, throughout CV, resources, report, F13 and the ERC brief. This is outside Annex V and avoids inventing an exception to the real call. As a companion clarification in call.md §2, spell out the imported compatibility restriction and first-doctorate cutoff before 1 January 2024 rather than leaving them only in the Article 8.2 reference. Preserve the existing type B task. If PID2024 is instead retained, merely correcting indirect costs to EUR 37500 awarded / EUR 21800 spent (totals EUR 187500 / EUR 109000) does not fix eligibility; that alternative needs a different eligible applicant or task pairing.

issues.where: data/public/dossiers/pollinator-heat-pi/dossier.yaml F08: “from 4.7 to 2.1 visits flower⁻¹ h⁻¹”; prior_project.md §3.3: “Overall visitation rate across all sites and weeks: 4.7”.
issues.problem: F08 assigns the pooled all-sites/all-weeks rate to the lowland non-heat-wave baseline. The source does not say that. A rounded 55% decrease to 2.1 suggests a baseline near 4.67 but does not establish the exact published pooled 4.7 as the lowland baseline. The fact.value substring audit passes because its value is only 55%; the semantic mismatch remains.
issues.fix: Replace F08.text with “During heat waves at 450 m, visitation was 2.1 visits flower⁻¹ h⁻¹, a 55% decline (95% CI 44–66%) relative to non-heat-wave weeks at that elevation.” Add a separate source-linked fact for the all-sites/all-weeks mean 4.7 visits flower⁻¹ h⁻¹ (SE 0.3). Do not supply an exact lowland baseline that is not in the visible report.

issues.where: data/public/dossiers/pollinator-heat-pi/prior_project.md, §§2–4: “Four permanent plots along an elevation gradient”; “Network metrics were computed separately for heat-wave weeks and non-heat-wave weeks”; numerical confidence intervals and “declined significantly”.
issues.problem: There is only one plot at each elevation, so elevation is completely confounded with site. Network connectance/NODF also depend on sampling completeness, while the report separates heat-wave from ordinary weeks without specifying effort/completeness adjustment. Its limitations mention one mountain range and three heat waves but omit the absence of independent elevation replication. This materially affects whether a new proposal can describe the observed elevation gradient as evidence of general buffering rather than four site-specific associations. The supplied summaries do not establish that the reported confidence intervals are numerically wrong; their analysis unit and calculation cannot be verified.
issues.fix: Add to limitations and the hidden registry: “One plot was sampled at each elevation; elevation and site are confounded. These are exploratory within-site heat-wave associations, not a replicated causal estimate of elevation buffering. The present report does not document effort/completeness standardisation or the sampling unit used for its confidence intervals; network robustness to unequal sampling completeness remains unverified.” Qualify the elevation-buffering interpretation accordingly. Retain the reported point estimates and uncertainty as reported exploratory summaries; do not invent a resampling procedure or delete intervals solely because raw data are unavailable. New proposals should treat replicated sites and effort-standardised network comparison as prospective validation.
